headline: Meet the Amazon's Laziest Frog, Newly Named to Science
meta_description: Scientists describe Adenomera varcena, a tiny Amazon frog distinguished by its unusually slow call—just 1-5 notes per minute instead of up to 70.
summary_short: Researchers in Brazil and Ecuador have identified a new frog species whose slowest-in-genus call sets it apart from look-alike relatives.
body:
A newly described species of tiny brown frog from the Amazonian floodplains of Ecuador and northwestern Brazil has earned an unlikely distinction: the slowest song in its genus. Named Adenomera varcena, the frog measures just 22 to 24 millimeters long and looks nearly identical to its relatives, yet its call tells a different evolutionary story. While related species typically vocalize at rates up to 70 notes a minute, A. varcena produces only one to five notes per minute, each lasting less than a tenth of a second. "It's as if the frog is feeling lazy," said lead author Marianna Borburema, now a researcher at the University of São Paulo, who spent three weeks analyzing the species' sounds. The discovery reveals how natural selection shapes frogs not through appearance but through the very traits that matter for survival: the call that attracts potential mates.

Scientists identified A. varcena as one of nine genetically distinct groups within what was previously thought to be a single species complex. The breakthrough came through DNA analysis and field work near the upper Juruá River in Brazil, where researchers collected samples from the seasonally flooded forests. Notably, A. varcena is the only member of its lineage adapted to floodplain living; all its closest relatives inhabit dry land forests, suggesting this species evolved its distinctive acoustic signature in response to a different environment.

Borburema emphasized the importance of recognizing even the smallest, most inconspicuous species. "A species can only be protected if it is known," she said. Her passion for the understated frog—one she calls beautiful and super cute despite its plain brown appearance—underscores a broader truth in conservation: significance lies not in glamour, but in uniqueness and the stories evolution tells through the smallest of voices.
quick_facts: Adenomera varcena sings just 1-5 notes per minute, slowest in its genus
New species found in Amazonian floodplains of Ecuador and northwestern Brazil
Frog measures 22-24 millimeters long with brown skin and dark patterns
Only species in its lineage adapted to seasonal floodplain forests
Identified as distinct through DNA analysis by Brazilian and international scientists
